q: Which statement best describes how LLMOps differs from MLOps for a team calling a hosted model API?
options: The main artefact is trained weights that need a model registry
The shipped unit is a bundle of prompt, model id, retrieval and tools, with free-text evaluation
CI/CD is unnecessary because the provider hosts the model
why: The bundle is the unit of change and evaluation is fuzzy. Weights registries matter only if you train; CI/CD is still needed.

q: A provider silently updates the model behind an alias and your answers change with no deploy. What is the best structural protection?
options: Pin an explicit model version and re-run evals before moving it
why: Pinning makes upstream change a deliberate, evaluated release. Retries and caching do not address behaviour drift.

q: Which is a characteristic risk of agents more than of a plain RAG pipeline?
options: Long-tail cost and latency from variable loop counts
why: Agent loops vary in length so a few runs can be very expensive; RAG issues like staleness exist but are not unique to agents.

q: Why should the model name live in validated configuration instead of in code?
options: It hides the model from logs
The same image can run in each environment, experiments change config, and bad values fail at start-up
why: Config separation lets one artefact be promoted across environments and makes change auditable; speed and hiding are irrelevant.

q: Which practice best protects against silent behaviour drift from dependencies?
options: Lockfile, pinned base image and pinned model id with eval-gated upgrades
why: Pinning plus gated upgrades makes any change deliberate. Temperature zero does not control version changes.

q: What is the main risk of tuning prompts against a single static eval set for months?
options: Overfitting and staleness so scores rise while real quality does not
The set becomes too fast to run
why: Repeated tuning on the same cases fits them. Use held-out data and refresh from production.

q: You tuned top-k, prompt and model together and the score improved. What is the best next step?
options: Run ablations changing one factor at a time to attribute the gain
Increase the eval set judge temperature
why: Changing several variables prevents attribution and some may hurt. Ablations reveal which help and cost.

q: What is the main benefit of moving a registry label instead of redeploying to roll back a prompt?
options: Fast, no build or deploy, limited by cache TTL
why: Label moves are pointer changes; they do not revert code and versions remain. Cache TTL bounds speed.

q: Your registry goes down and requests start failing. Which design would have prevented the outage?
options: Cached last-known-good plus a bundled fallback prompt
Fetching on every request with no timeout
Storing prompts only in a notebook
why: Caching and a bundled fallback remove the hard runtime dependency.

q: Why record the baseline's run-to-run variation?
options: To tell whether a candidate's small gain exceeds noise
To fix the seed in the provider
why: Non-deterministic scoring produces a noise band; gains inside it are not evidence.

q: A faithfulness metric is low while contextual recall is high. Where is the likely fault?
options: Generation: prompt or model is not staying grounded in the context
why: High recall means the right context arrived; low faithfulness means the answer departed from it.

q: Which approach best reduces flakiness of an LLM-judged gate?
options: Use exact-string match for free text
Aggregate thresholds, pinned judge, low temperature and repeats on borderline cases
why: Aggregation and repeats reduce chance flips; exact match breaks on legitimate paraphrase.

q: What is the best use of a fast smoke subset?
options: Give quick PR feedback on critical cases while the full suite gates release
why: Tiering balances speed and coverage; the full gate still protects production.

q: Why is a single global threshold across all metrics a poor design?
options: Metrics differ in scale, noise and risk
why: Different metrics have different baselines and consequences, so bars should be set per metric.

q: Why enforce an agent's step and spend limits in code rather than in the prompt?
options: The model or an injected instruction can ignore prompt rules
why: Prompts are advisory; deterministic enforcement outside the model cannot be talked around.

q: A schema-validation loop keeps failing for one prompt version. What is the sensible handling?
options: Cap re-asks, fall back cleanly, log the failure rate by version and investigate
why: Bounded retries control cost and the rising failure rate flags a regression.

q: What is the best way to introduce a new guardrail with unknown false-positive rate?
options: Run in shadow mode, measure on real traffic, then enforce with a tuned threshold
Apply it to 100% and wait for tickets
why: Shadow mode reveals false positives and latency without harming users.

q: Why do you need to check retrieved documents for injection?
options: Untrusted text in context can carry indirect injection
why: Indirect injection arrives through retrieved or tool content that the model reads as instructions.

q: Behind a proxy, users see the whole answer arrive at once instead of streaming. What is the most likely cause?
why: Buffering at the proxy collects the stream; disable buffering for SSE routes.

q: Why should a readiness probe avoid calling the LLM provider?
options: It cannot be done over HTTP
Cost, rate limits and an outage would drop every instance simultaneously
why: Cascading unreadiness during a provider blip turns a partial outage into total outage.

q: Which Dockerfile ordering gives the best rebuild speed?
options: Install dependencies from a copied lockfile, then copy source
Copy all source, then install dependencies
why: Dependencies change rarely; caching that layer avoids reinstalling on every code change.

q: A client disconnects mid-stream but the server keeps generating. What is the main consequence?
options: Wasted token spend and held concurrency
why: Without cancellation you pay for output nobody reads and occupy capacity.

q: Where should production API keys come from?
options: A secret store or runtime environment using the instance role
why: Runtime injection avoids leaking secrets in images or history.

q: What is the main reason to tag images with the commit SHA?
why: A SHA identifies precisely what was built; latest does not.

q: Which GitHub Actions feature pauses a production deploy until a person approves?
why: Protected environments with reviewers hold the job and release environment secrets after approval.

q: Why is OIDC to AWS preferred over stored access keys?
options: Short-lived credentials with scoped roles, nothing long-lived to leak
It is faster to run tests
It removes the need for IAM
why: OIDC issues temporary credentials; stored keys can leak and need rotation.

q: Streams die at precisely 60 seconds behind the load balancer. What is the best first fix?
options: Raise the idle timeout and send SSE keep-alives
why: The default idle timeout closes quiet connections; keep-alives and a longer timeout address it.

q: Which scaling signal best fits an I/O-bound LLM gateway?
why: CPU stays low while waiting on providers; in-flight streams show true load.

q: Provider returns many 429s during a traffic spike. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Shared rate limiting, backoff with jitter, load shedding and bounded scaling
Scale to the maximum instance count
why: Quota is shared, so more instances amplify the problem; control demand instead.

q: Why prefer blue/green for a streaming app despite higher cost?
options: Fast rollback and near-zero downtime, with draining for in-flight streams
why: Traffic switch with draining and kept old environment gives safe quick rollback.

q: Which alert is best aligned with the principle 'page only when a human must act'?
options: p95 time-to-first-token above SLO for 10 minutes
Disk read spike for one second
why: Symptom-based, sustained, user-affecting condition; the others are noise.

q: Why is a user_id label on a Prometheus metric a problem?
options: Unbounded cardinality creates a series per user and exhausts memory
why: Each label value is a distinct series; per-user detail belongs in traces.

q: What does tracing add that Prometheus metrics alone do not?
options: Per-request step-by-step detail including prompts and retrieved context
why: Metrics show that something is wrong; traces show which request and why.

q: Why should production failures be added to the eval suite?
options: To prevent the same regression from silently returning
why: Regression cases make the gate enforce lessons from incidents.

q: Quality dropped right after a prompt promotion. What is the fastest safe mitigation?
options: Move the production label back to the previous version
why: Label rollback is quick and low-risk; the others do not address the cause.

q: Which outcome best reflects a good blameless review of an LLM incident?
options: Regression eval case, new alert and a rollback lever, each with an owner
why: Concrete systemic actions prevent recurrence; blame and vague advice do not.

q: Why re-run the full eval suite before adopting a new model version?
options: Behaviour, cost and latency can differ and prompts tuned for one model may regress on another
It removes the need for monitoring
why: Model changes are releases; only your own data shows impact on your tasks.

q: Which three artefacts must you pin and record so an eval gate is replayable?
options: Temperature, batch size, and GPU type
Prompt version, product model snapshot, and judge plus rubric
Docker tag, domain name, and TLS cert
Grafana board, Slack channel, and on-call
why: Prompts, product models, and judges all move. A floating judge creates fake regressions.

q: A policy-touching prompt is green on the suite. What else should block a silent production flip?
options: A named human review on the versioned artefact
Turning off traces to save cost
why: Not every change is a silent deploy. Policy wording needs a recorded approver after the gate.

q: What should a prompt feature flag store?
options: The raw prompt text for that tenant
A pointer to a versioned prompt id or label
why: Flags select a version so you can flip back without a rebuild. They are not a paste bin.

q: Faithfulness is up but the billing parser throws after a prompt change. What was missing?
options: Contract tests on the output schema in CI
why: Schema contracts catch missing or mistyped fields that quality judges can still pass.

q: Why version the golden set as carefully as the prompt?
options: So object storage bills go up
So a score names the exam it sat and you cannot quietly rewrite labels to pass
why: A score is a pair of system plus exam. An unversioned set lets you fake a win.

q: Dev, staging, and prod should share which of the following?
options: The same eval command and gold-set id
why: Approvals tighten; the exam does not get friendlier. Same command, same set.

q: You want to try a new prompt on live traffic with an instant undo. What do you do first?
options: Rebuild the image with the text hard-coded
Canary the versioned prompt to about 5 percent and watch quality and cost
Switch the production alias to latest
why: A 5 percent canary on a labelled version lets you flip back without a rebuild.

q: What is a model shadow used for?
options: Scoring a candidate pin on live traffic without showing users the new answers
why: Shadow scores the new model on real inputs while users still see the current pin.

q: Why implement input and output filters as code rather than only a system prompt?
options: Code can fail closed, be tested, and logged; a prompt is best-effort
Code is always faster than a model
why: Policy that only lives in a prompt will be argued with. A deny path in code will not.

q: Which pair is the best first defence against a runaway agent and a abusive client?
options: Bigger GPUs and a longer timeout
Step/spend caps and rate limits per user and per tool
Turning off traces and raising k
why: Caps stop loops; per-user and per-tool limits stop abuse. Both are LLMOps.

q: Faithfulness moved after a Friday release that changed prompt, pin, and the crawl. What process failed?
options: You should have changed one lever and isolated which one moved the metric
You should have deleted the gold set
You should have disabled health checks
You should have baked keys into the image
why: Prompt vs model vs data changes must be isolated or the metric has no owner.

q: What makes an eval run reproducible next month?
options: The same snapshot, gold-set version, and seed or sampling policy
A new laptop and latest aliases
why: Reproducible runs need the same snapshot, set, and seed policy — not a fresh latest.

q: Where should the eval suite run in GitHub Actions?
options: As an optional notebook someone remembers
As a required check before the image is built and pushed
why: Eval is a required check, not a manual notebook, and it sits before the push.

q: How should the pipeline get cloud credentials?
options: Print long-lived keys in the workflow YAML logs
OIDC to assume a role, with keys kept out of action output
Email the key to the runner
why: OIDC means keys never appear in action output or fork builds.

q: You reverted the container after a bad release but answers are still wrong. What did rollback miss?
options: The prompt id or label that also moved
why: Reverting the container is not enough if the production prompt label stayed on the bad version.

q: What belongs in an incident note for an LLM outage?
options: Timeline, impact, and the pin or label you restored — no user text
The entire gold set pasted into Slack
why: Incident notes need timeline, impact, and the pin you restored — not user text.

q: What should sit on the same dashboard as p95 for an LLM app?
options: Faithfulness (or an equivalent quality score) and token cost
why: Quality and cost belong next to SRE signals or you will miss fluent failures.

q: What does trace-to-example mean?
options: One click from a bad answer to a new gold-set case
Printing the system prompt in the UI
why: A production miss should become an eval case without a scavenger hunt.

q: Which sequence is the capstone ops story?
options: Redesign the model, then rewrite the UI
Page, pull the matching lever, roll back, add the miss to the set
Hire a GPU vendor, then delete evals
why: The story is how you would page, roll back, and add the miss — not a new feature.

q: What fits on a one-page LLM runbook?
options: Prompt id, model pin, eval command, and who to call
Every vendor blog of the year
why: One page: ids, the command, the owner. Longer runbooks do not get opened.
